pinyin: zhèn xīng zhōng huá

meaning.en: A patriotic slogan calling for the rejuvenation and strengthening of the nation.
meaning.zh: 爱国口号，号召使国家复兴、繁荣强盛。

examples.zh: 他立志学好科学，为振兴中华贡献力量。
examples.en: He is determined to study science well and help revitalise China.

examples.zh: “振兴中华”的口号激励了一代又一代的青年。
examples.en: The slogan 'revitalise China' has inspired generation after generation of young people.

story.en: Sun Yat-sen founded the Revive China Society (兴中会) in Honolulu in 1894; its manifesto called on people to 'revitalise China'.
story.zh: 1894年孙中山在檀香山创立兴中会，宣言号召“振兴中华”。

usage.en: Formal, patriotic register, common in speeches, school essays and news. The slogan was first put forward by Sun Yat-sen in 1894.
usage.zh: 正式、爱国色彩，常见于演讲、作文和新闻。孙中山1894年创立兴中会时首先提出。

text: 革命尚未成功，同志仍须努力
pinyin: gé mìng shàng wèi chéng gōng, tóng zhì réng xū nǔ lì
literal: revolution · still · not yet · succeed · comrades · still · must · work hard
natural: the revolution has not yet succeeded; comrades must still work hard

meaning.en: Sun Yat-sen's dying exhortation: the goal is not yet reached, so the effort must continue; today quoted of any unfinished cause.
meaning.zh: 孙中山临终遗言的通行说法：目标尚未实现，大家仍须继续奋斗；今天也用来勉励人们未竟之业仍要努力。

equivalents: the work is not yet done

examples.zh: 项目虽然取得了阶段性成果，但革命尚未成功，同志仍须努力。
examples.en: The project has reached a milestone, but the work is not done and we must keep going.

examples.zh: 老师在黑板上写下“革命尚未成功，同志仍须努力”，勉励大家冲刺高考。
examples.en: The teacher wrote 'the revolution has not yet succeeded; comrades must still work hard' on the board to spur everyone on for the final sprint.

story.en: Sun Yat-sen's will, signed on 11 March 1925, the day before his death, was drafted by Wang Jingwei from his dictation; it ends by urging comrades to carry the revolution on.
story.zh: 1925年3月11日，孙中山病逝前一天签署遗嘱，由汪精卫根据其意思起草，嘱咐同志继续努力完成革命。

usage.en: Often quoted half-jokingly in workplaces and schools. The popular wording is a condensed form of the will's text 现在革命尚未成功，凡我同志，务须依照余所著……继续努力.
usage.zh: 常在职场、校园中半开玩笑地引用。通行说法是遗嘱原文“现在革命尚未成功，凡我同志，务须依照余所著……继续努力”的缩略。

text: 世界潮流，浩浩荡荡，顺之者昌，逆之者亡
pinyin: shì jiè cháo liú, hào hào dàng dàng, shùn zhī zhě chāng, nì zhī zhě wáng
literal: world · tide · mighty · mighty · follow · it · person · prosper · oppose · it · person · perish
natural: the tide of the world is mighty: those who go with it flourish, those who oppose it perish

meaning.en: Sun Yat-sen's motto: historical trends are irresistible, and those who go with them thrive while those who resist them are swept away.
meaning.zh: 孙中山题词：历史潮流不可阻挡，顺应者兴旺，违逆者衰亡。

equivalents: go with the tide of history
those who resist progress are left behind

examples.zh: 面对数字化浪潮，世界潮流，浩浩荡荡，顺之者昌，逆之者亡。
examples.en: Faced with the digital wave, the tide of the world is mighty: go with it or be left behind.

examples.zh: 领导引用“世界潮流，浩浩荡荡，顺之者昌，逆之者亡”，提醒大家要主动改革。
examples.en: The manager quoted 'the tide of the world is mighty' to remind everyone to reform of their own accord.

story.en: Sun Yat-sen wrote this couplet-like motto in calligraphy in 1916; it has been widely reproduced ever since.
story.zh: 1916年孙中山亲笔题写此语，后来广为流传。

usage.en: Often quoted in speeches about reform and globalisation. Commonly shortened to 浩浩荡荡 (see that entry) or 顺之者昌，逆之者亡. The calligraphy is dated 1916 and the wording echoes Mencius's 顺天者存，逆天者亡.
usage.zh: 常用于有关改革、全球化的讲话，也常截取后半句。题词写于1916年，语意近于《孟子》“顺天者存，逆天者亡”。

pinyin: qū chú dá lǔ, huī fù zhōng huá
natural: drive out the Tatars, restore China

meaning.en: An anti-Qing revolutionary slogan that called for ending Manchu rule; today a historical reference.
meaning.zh: 反清革命口号，主张推翻满洲统治；今天多作历史典故提及。

examples.zh: 历史课上讲到同盟会的纲领：驱除鞑虏，恢复中华，创立民国，平均地权。
examples.en: The history class covered the Revolutionary Alliance's programme: drive out the Tatars, restore China, found a republic and equalise land rights.

examples.zh: “驱除鞑虏，恢复中华”是辛亥革命前流行的口号。
examples.en: 'Drive out the Tatars, restore China' was a popular slogan before the 1911 Revolution.

origin.source: 孙中山，中国同盟会纲领（1905年）

story.en: The first of the four points in the 1905 Revolutionary Alliance (同盟会) programme drafted by Sun Yat-sen; the slogan was used by earlier secret societies and by the Ming founder's 1367 proclamation.
story.zh: 1905年中国同盟会纲领“驱除鞑虏，恢复中华，创立民国，平均地权”的第一条；此语早为会党所用，朱元璋1367年檄文亦有近似说法。

usage.en: A historical slogan; 鞑虏 was a derogatory term for northern peoples, here the Manchus, and Sun later spoke of unity of the five peoples. Not used in modern speech except about the 1911 era.
usage.zh: 属历史口号。“鞑虏”本是对北方民族的蔑称，这里指满洲统治者；孙中山后来主张五族共和。今天只用于谈论辛亥时期。

pinyin: gēng zhě yǒu qí tián

meaning.en: A land-reform principle: those who farm the land should own it.
meaning.zh: 土地改革的原则：种地的人应拥有土地。

examples.zh: 历史书上说，孙中山提出“耕者有其田”，主张解决农民的土地问题。
examples.en: The history book says Sun Yat-sen advocated 'land to the tiller' to solve the peasants' land problem.

examples.zh: 几十年前的土地改革，目标就是耕者有其田。
examples.en: The aim of the land reform decades ago was that the tiller should own the land.

origin.source: 孙中山《民生主义》演讲（1924年）

story.en: In his 1924 lectures on the Principle of People's Livelihood Sun Yat-sen stated that 'the tiller should have his own field' as the solution to the farmers' problem.
story.zh: 孙中山1924年讲《民生主义》时明确提出“耕者有其田”，作为解决农民问题的办法。

usage.en: Used when discussing land reform in China and Taiwan (the Land-to-the-Tiller Act of 1953). Formal.
usage.zh: 谈及中国大陆和台湾土地改革（1953年台湾《耕者有其田条例》）时使用，正式。

pinyin: yǒu qiāng biàn shì cǎo tóu wáng
literal: have · gun · then · is · grass-head · king
natural: whoever has guns is a self-made king

meaning.en: Whoever commands armed men can set himself up as a local ruler; a comment on the warlord period.
meaning.zh: 谁有武装谁就能称霸一方，多形容军阀混战的乱世。

equivalents: he who has the guns makes the rules

examples.zh: 军阀割据的年代，有枪便是草头王。
examples.en: In the warlord years, whoever had guns made himself a king.

examples.zh: 纪录片讲到当年有枪便是草头王的乱象。
examples.en: The documentary dealt with the chaos in which anyone with guns was a petty king.

usage.en: 草头王 means a self-styled chieftain or bandit king. Casual, critical; used of warlordism or any rule by force.
usage.zh: “草头王”指自立为王的草莽首领。口语，带批评意味，用于军阀割据或以武力称霸的情形。

pinyin: yǒu nǎi biàn shì niáng

meaning.en: Used of people who give loyalty to whoever pays them, with no principles of their own.
meaning.zh: 指人没有原则，谁给好处就认谁，谁给钱就跟谁。

examples.zh: 他有奶便是娘，哪家出价高就替哪家卖命。
examples.en: He has no loyalty but to whoever pays; he works for the highest bidder.

examples.zh: 这些雇佣兵有奶便是娘，没有真正的立场。
examples.en: These mercenaries follow whoever pays and have no real conviction.

usage.en: Often paired with 有枪便是草头王 in describing the warlord era and its hired loyalties. Derogatory, casual. Compare the 歇后语 婴儿饿肚皮——有奶便是娘.
usage.zh: 常与“有枪便是草头王”并说，形容军阀时代以利相从的作风。贬义，口语。另见歇后语“婴儿饿肚皮——有奶便是娘”。

pinyin: chéng tóu biàn huàn dà wáng qí
literal: city · wall-top · change · flicker · great · king · banner
natural: on the city wall the warlords' banners keep changing

meaning.en: Rulers and regimes change again and again amid war and chaos; a line about the warlord years.
meaning.zh: 形容军阀混战、政权频繁更迭的乱世。

examples.zh: 那几年战乱不断，真是城头变幻大王旗。
examples.en: Those years were full of war, with new masters raising their flags over the town again and again.

examples.zh: 这家公司一年换了三个老板，城头变幻大王旗。
examples.en: The firm has had three owners in a year; the banners on the wall keep changing.

origin.source: 鲁迅《无题》（“惯于长夜过春时”，1931年）

story.en: From Lu Xun's poem written in 1931 after the execution of young leftist writers: '惯于长夜过春时，挈妇将雏鬓有丝。梦里依稀慈母泪，城头变幻大王旗。'
story.zh: 出自鲁迅1931年悼念被害青年作家所作七律：“惯于长夜过春时，挈妇将雏鬓有丝。梦里依稀慈母泪，城头变幻大王旗。”

usage.en: Quoted as a literary description of chaotic changes of power; today also used jokingly of frequent management reshuffles.
usage.zh: 多用来形容政权更替频繁、局势混乱，现在也半开玩笑地形容公司领导层频繁更换。

pinyin: dà pào yī xiǎng, huáng jīn wàn liǎng
literal: big · cannon · one · fire · gold · ten-thousand · taels
natural: when the cannon fires, ten thousand taels of gold

meaning.en: Wartime brings huge profits for arms dealers and other sellers; also a cynical comment on those who gain from conflict.
meaning.zh: 战争一打响，军火商等就能大发其财；也用来讥讽靠战争获利的人。

equivalents: a good war for those who sell the guns

examples.zh: 大炮一响，黄金万两，军火商最盼望战事爆发。
examples.en: When the cannons fire the gold comes in, and arms dealers long for war.

examples.zh: 老人说，大炮一响，黄金万两，但死的是老百姓。
examples.en: The old man said war brings fortunes to some, but ordinary people pay with their lives.

usage.en: A popular saying with no certain author, widely heard in the Republican era; often used with a sceptical tone, and also to refer to wartime spending.
usage.zh: 没有确切出处的俗语，民国时期广为流传，语气多带讥讽，也指战时开支带动的盈利。

pinyin: dé xiān shēng hé sài xiān shēng

meaning.en: The slogan of the New Culture Movement: democracy (德谟克拉西) and science (赛因斯) as the means to modernise China.
meaning.zh: 新文化运动口号：以民主和科学作为中国现代化的两大旗帜。

examples.zh: 五四运动高举“德先生和赛先生”两面大旗。
examples.en: The May Fourth Movement raised the two banners of Mr Democracy and Mr Science.

examples.zh: 讲到新文化运动，不能不提德先生和赛先生。
examples.en: One cannot discuss the New Culture Movement without mentioning Mr Democracy and Mr Science.

origin.source: 陈独秀《本志罪案之答辩书》（《新青年》，1919年）

story.en: Chen Duxiu defended the journal New Youth by saying that only 'Mr Democracy and Mr Science' could save China from its dark political and moral state.
story.zh: 陈独秀1919年在《新青年》上答辩时写道，只有拥护“德先生”和“赛先生”，才能救治中国政治上、道德上的黑暗。

usage.en: Formal; still used in speeches about reform, education and the legacy of 1919.
usage.zh: 正式用语，仍常用于谈改革、教育和五四精神的讲话。

pinyin: dǎ dǎo kǒng jiā diàn

meaning.en: A New Culture Movement slogan attacking Confucian orthodoxy and its role in holding back reform.
meaning.zh: 新文化运动口号，批判儒家正统观念对社会变革的束缚。

examples.zh: 五四时期有人喊出“打倒孔家店”，但并非全盘否定孔子。
examples.en: Some cried 'knock down the Confucian shop' in the May Fourth era, though not everyone rejected Confucius entirely.

examples.zh: 论文讨论“打倒孔家店”口号的由来和影响。
examples.en: The paper discusses the origin and impact of the 'knock down the Confucian shop' slogan.

usage.en: Historical slogan, popularised in the New Culture Movement and linked to Wu Yu and Hu Shih (who praised Wu as the 'old hero who attacked the Confucian shop'). Today a historical reference; scholars stress that the target was the state-backed doctrine, not Confucius himself.
usage.zh: 新文化运动时期流行的口号，与吴虞、胡适有关（胡适称吴虞为“只手打孔家店的老英雄”）。今天多作历史提法；学界强调批判对象是被官方利用的儒家教条，而非孔子本人。

pinyin: quán pán xī huà

meaning.en: The view that China should adopt Western culture and institutions wholesale; also used critically of copying foreign ways without thought.
meaning.zh: 主张中国全面采用西方文化和制度的观点；也批评不加思考地照搬外国做法。

examples.zh: 三十年代，陈序经等人提倡全盘西化，引发了激烈争论。
examples.en: In the 1930s Chen Xujing and others advocated wholesale Westernisation, which sparked heated debate.

examples.zh: 传统与现代并非只有全盘西化一条路。
examples.en: Wholesale Westernisation is not the only path between tradition and modernity.

usage.en: A term from the Republic-era culture debates (notably 陈序经 and 胡适 in the 1930s). Mostly used critically today; neutral in historical writing.
usage.zh: 民国时期文化论战中的用语（三十年代陈序经、胡适等）。今天多作批评之词，历史论述中则中性。

pinyin: wài zhēng zhǔ quán, nèi chú guó zéi
literal: outwardly · fight for · sovereignty · inwardly · remove · national · traitors
natural: fight for sovereignty abroad, remove the traitors at home

meaning.en: The May Fourth demonstration slogan of 1919: resist foreign encroachment and punish officials seen as selling out the nation.
meaning.zh: 1919年五四运动的口号：对外争取国家主权，对内惩办卖国官僚。

examples.zh: 五四游行的标语写着“外争主权，内除国贼”。
examples.en: The banners of the May Fourth march read 'fight for sovereignty abroad, remove the traitors at home'.

examples.zh: 课文讲到学生们高呼“外争主权，内除国贼”。
examples.en: The lesson tells how students shouted 'fight for sovereignty abroad, remove the traitors at home'.

usage.en: A historical slogan of the May Fourth Movement (1919), directed against the Paris Peace Conference decision on Shandong and three pro-Japan officials. Formal, historical reference.
usage.zh: 五四运动（1919年）的历史口号，针对巴黎和会关于山东的决定和三名亲日官员。正式，多作历史提法。

pinyin: wù wàng guó chǐ

meaning.en: A call to remember the nation's humiliations, especially the wrongs done by foreign powers, and to strive for strength.
meaning.zh: 提醒人们铭记国家受过的屈辱，尤其是外国列强造成的伤害，发愤图强。

examples.zh: 博物馆的墙上写着“勿忘国耻”四个大字。
examples.en: The words 'never forget national humiliation' are written large on the museum wall.

examples.zh: 每逢纪念日，学校都组织学生勿忘国耻，振兴中华。
examples.en: On each anniversary the school asks pupils to remember the nation's humiliation and work for its revival.

usage.en: Originally a slogan of 9 May 1915, marked as National Humiliation Day after the Twenty-One Demands; later used for Japan's invasion as well. Formal, commemorative.
usage.zh: 最初是1915年“五九国耻”的口号，因日本提出“二十一条”要求；后来也用于纪念抗日战争等。正式，多用于纪念场合。

pinyin: shí yè jiù guó

meaning.en: The view, popular in late Qing and early Republic, that building modern industry would make China strong.
meaning.zh: 清末民初流行的主张：通过发展近代工业使国家富强。

examples.zh: 张謇兴办纱厂，提倡实业救国。
examples.en: Zhang Jian set up cotton mills, advocating the saving of the nation through industry.

examples.zh: 他放弃了学业，一心想着实业救国。
examples.en: He gave up his studies, intent on saving the country through industry.

usage.en: A historical idea tied to figures such as 张謇 and 荣氏兄弟; today used in historical discussion or as a sincere motto of private entrepreneurs.
usage.zh: 与张謇、荣氏兄弟等人物相联系的历史主张；今天用于历史讨论，或作民营企业家的自勉之语。

pinyin: ruò guó wú wài jiāo
natural: a weak nation has no diplomacy

meaning.en: A nation without strength cannot make its voice count in international affairs.
meaning.zh: 国家实力不强，在国际事务中就没有发言权。

equivalents: a weak country has no say

examples.zh: 历史告诉我们，弱国无外交，要想有尊严就得自强。
examples.en: History shows that a weak country gets no hearing, so self-strengthening is the way to dignity.

examples.zh: 巴黎和会上中国的遭遇，让人感叹弱国无外交。
examples.en: China's treatment at the Paris Peace Conference made people lament that weak nations have no diplomacy.

usage.en: Often linked to the Paris Peace Conference of 1919 and the treaties of the late Qing; used in discussions of national strength and foreign policy. The exact origin is not certain.
usage.zh: 常与1919年巴黎和会、晚清不平等条约联系在一起，用于谈论国力与外交。确切出处不详。

pinyin: lǐ jiào chī rén

meaning.en: A New Culture Movement criticism that rigid feudal ethics oppressed people, especially women and the young.
meaning.zh: 新文化运动对僵化的封建礼教压迫人（尤其是妇女和青年）的批判。

examples.zh: 《狂人日记》写出了礼教吃人的本质。
examples.en: 'Diary of a Madman' exposes the cannibalistic nature of the old code of ethics.

examples.zh: 旧时守节的故事，今天看来是礼教吃人。
examples.en: Stories of lifelong widowhood in the old days look today like the old ethics devouring people.

story.en: In the story, a narrator sees that the history books written with 'benevolence and morality' really say 'eat people' on every page.
story.zh: 小说中，“狂人”发现满本历史上写着“仁义道德”，字缝里却满是“吃人”二字。

usage.en: A summary of the idea in Lu Xun's story; Lu Xun himself has the narrator read 仁义道德 and find the words 'eat people' between the lines. Also stated as 吃人的礼教 by Wu Yu in 1919. Formal, critical.
usage.zh: 这是对鲁迅小说主题的概括：小说中狂人从“仁义道德”的字缝里看出“吃人”二字。吴虞1919年也有“吃人的礼教”之说。正式，批判性。

pinyin: jiù jiù hái zi

meaning.en: A plea to rescue the young from harmful influences and an oppressive upbringing; now used for children's welfare and education.
meaning.zh: 呼吁把年轻一代从有害的影响和压抑的教育中解救出来；今天也用于关注儿童福利和教育。

examples.zh: 看到孩子们被作业压得喘不过气，有人喊出：救救孩子。
examples.en: Seeing children crushed by homework, some people cried out: save the children.

examples.zh: 这篇文章以“救救孩子”为题，呼吁改革应试教育。
examples.en: The article is titled 'Save the Children' and calls for reform of exam-oriented education.

story.en: The last line of Lu Xun's story: 'Perhaps there are still children who have not eaten people? Save the children...'
story.zh: 《狂人日记》结尾：“没有吃过人的孩子，或者还有？救救孩子……”

usage.en: Neutral to literary; often used as an emotional headline in education debates.
usage.zh: 中性偏书面，常作教育讨论中的呼吁性标题。

pinyin: āi qí bù xìng, nù qí bù zhēng
literal: pity · his · misfortune · be angry at · his · not · strive
natural: pity their misfortune, rage at their lack of fight

meaning.en: To feel sorrow for someone's plight but anger that they do not stand up for themselves.
meaning.zh: 既同情他的不幸，又恼恨他不奋起抗争。

equivalents: pity their plight but be angry at their passivity
sorry for them, angry at them

examples.zh: 看着那些甘于现状的朋友，他哀其不幸，怒其不争。
examples.en: Seeing friends content with their lot, he pitied them and was angry that they would not fight.

examples.zh: 鲁迅对国民性的批评，正是哀其不幸，怒其不争。
examples.en: Lu Xun's criticism of the national character was one of pity for their misfortune and anger at their passivity.

story.en: Lu Xun describes how Byron felt toward the Greeks he fought for: he 'pitied their misfortune and was angry at their lack of fight'.
story.zh: 鲁迅在论拜伦时写道，拜伦对他为之而战的希腊人，既“哀其不幸”，又“怒其不争”。

usage.en: Often used of a person who is in difficulty but does nothing to help themselves, especially in essays and about family or students. Literary, from Lu Xun.
usage.zh: 多用于形容处境不好却不图振作的人，常见于作文，也用于说家人和学生。书面语，出自鲁迅。

pinyin: jīng shén shèng lì fǎ

meaning.en: Comforting oneself by imagining a victory in the mind when one has actually been beaten or humiliated.
meaning.zh: 遭到失败或屈辱时，在心里想象自己获胜，以此自我安慰。

examples.zh: 他输了比赛还说对手不配赢，这是精神胜利法。
examples.en: He lost the game and said the opponent didn't deserve to win; that is Ah Q-style spiritual victory.

examples.zh: 网上有人用精神胜利法自我安慰，其实问题并没有解决。
examples.en: Some people online console themselves with imagined victories, but the problem is not solved.

story.en: Ah Q, beaten and mocked, always finds a way to feel superior, for instance telling himself, when beaten, that it is just 'a son hitting his father'.
story.zh: 阿Q挨打受辱后总能找到办法觉得自己高人一等，例如自认为“儿子打老子”。

usage.en: Refers to the habit of the title character in Lu Xun's novella 《阿Q正传》 (1921), who 'wins' every humiliation in his mind. Negative; often just 阿Q精神.
usage.zh: 指鲁迅《阿Q正传》（1921年）中阿Q的习惯：每受一次屈辱，就在心里“胜利”一次。贬义，也说“阿Q精神”。

pinyin: yú wú shēng chù tīng jīng léi
literal: in · no · sound · place · hear · startling · thunder

meaning.en: To perceive great change or a powerful force beneath apparent quiet.
meaning.zh: 在表面的沉寂中听到惊天动地的巨变将临。

examples.zh: 于无声处听惊雷，微小的变化里藏着时代的大潮。
examples.en: Hear thunder in the silence: the tide of an era hides in tiny changes.

examples.zh: 那场演讲让人于无声处听惊雷。
examples.en: The speech made people hear thunder in the silence.

usage.en: Often credited to Lu Xun, from the mood of 《无声的中国》 (1927: '不在沉默中爆发，就在沉默中灭亡'), but the wording is not found there. It was popularised as the title of Zong Fuxian's 1978 play 《于无声处》. Literary, much used in essays and headlines.
usage.zh: 常被说成鲁迅所言，其意近于《无声的中国》（1927年）“不在沉默中爆发，就在沉默中灭亡”，但原文并无此语。1978年宗福先话剧《于无声处》使它广为流传。书面语，常用于文章和标题。

pinyin: duǒ jìn xiǎo lóu chéng yī tǒng
literal: hide · into · small · house · form · one · whole
natural: hide in a small attic and make it a world of one's own

meaning.en: To shut oneself away from the turmoil outside and live in a little world of one's own; sometimes used of wilful detachment.
meaning.zh: 躲在自己的小天地里，不理会外界的纷扰；有时指刻意回避现实。

equivalents: retreat into one's own little world

examples.zh: 他躲进小楼成一统，不问世事，只管读书。
examples.en: He retreated into his little attic, ignoring the world and just reading.

examples.zh: 疫情期间，许多人躲进小楼成一统，在家过起了慢生活。
examples.en: During the pandemic many people shut themselves in their own little worlds and lived at a slower pace at home.

story.en: From Lu Xun's poem: '运交华盖欲何求，未敢翻身已碰头…横眉冷对千夫指，俯首甘为孺子牛。躲进小楼成一统，管他冬夏与春秋。'
story.zh: 出自鲁迅1932年所作《自嘲》：“运交华盖欲何求，未敢翻身已碰头…横眉冷对千夫指，俯首甘为孺子牛。躲进小楼成一统，管他冬夏与春秋。”

usage.en: Often used half-jokingly of working from home or hobbyists in their own corner. In the poem Lu Xun uses it ironically of his own forced seclusion in Shanghai.
usage.zh: 常半开玩笑地形容在家工作或沉迷小圈子的人。鲁迅在诗中带着自嘲，写自己在上海被迫隐居。

pinyin: zhí miàn cǎn dàn de rén shēng
natural: to look squarely at a bleak life

meaning.en: To face harsh reality with courage instead of avoiding it.
meaning.zh: 勇敢面对残酷的现实，不回避。

examples.zh: 成长就是学会直面惨淡的人生。
examples.en: Growing up means learning to face a bleak life squarely.

examples.zh: 她选择直面惨淡的人生，重新开始。
examples.en: She chose to face a harsh life squarely and start again.

story.en: Lu Xun mourned a student killed in the 18 March 1926 shooting: 'A true brave man dares to face a bleak life, dares to look at streaming blood.'
story.zh: 1926年鲁迅悼念“三一八”惨案中遇难的学生刘和珍：“真的猛士，敢于直面惨淡的人生，敢于正视淋漓的鲜血。”

usage.en: Often quoted with the following line 敢于正视淋漓的鲜血. Literary, inspirational, a favourite of school essays.
usage.zh: 常与下句“敢于正视淋漓的鲜血”连用。书面语，励志色彩，是作文常用语。
